newsitem.title: JAPAN: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks to try upside cautiously.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks to try upside cautiously.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to test the upside cautiously this week, backed by investor demand in a wider range of issues, including steel and chemical shares.
But profit-taking pressure is still strong, which could slow any rise in the key index above 18,500, brokers said.
On Friday, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 18,352.14, up 505.16 points or 2.8 percent from its close on April 11. It had advanced for four consecutive days.
"The firm tone will continue and the Nikkei 225 is likely to test 19,000," said Hiroyuki Nakai, chief investment strategist at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
But Kazuo Shiogai, deputy branch manager at ING Baring Securities (Japan) Ltd, said there would be a line of selling above 18,000.
"The Nikkei 225 would have to survive solid selling above 18,000," he said. "It would trade in a narrow range between 17,500 and 18,500 for another week," he said.

Brokers said a halt in the yen's decline against the dollar kept investors from further chasing blue-chip issues, which have already reached high price levels, turning their eyes to other lower-priced shares of raw material companies.
There is growing caution over currency intervention, and that would cap any sharp rally in the dollar, they said.

On Friday, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Ministry of Finance's International Finance Bureau, told Reuters that forex intervention is most effective when done unexpectedly and that Japan won't conduct "defensive" intervention.
"The weak yen had propelled buying in electricals and automobiles, and now it's helping raw materials -- this is a second round of buying," Nikko's Nakai said.
"Especially steel and chemicals -- which are backed by good earnings and a low PER (price-earnings ratio) -- are buys," he said.
Recent buying by pension funds of a wide range of issues after a new financial year began on April 1 will continue to support market sentiment, brokers also said.
The list of heavily traded issues was dominated by steel companies and banks on Friday.
Nippon Steel Corp topped the list, with 11.91 million shares traded. The share price gained one yen to 358.
It was followed by Kawasaki Steel Corp, with 9.52 million shares traded. The firm's shares rose seven yen to 371, a high for the calendar year.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd was the third heaviest traded, gaining four yen to 245, followed by Sumitomo Bank Ltd, which rose 100 yen to 1,460, and Sakura Bank Ltd, which ended 19 yen higher at 690.
